subject: Suspected data exposure — request for incident evidence & subprocessor details
messages:
From: Alice Zhang <alice@finexcorp.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.example.com
Cc: tom.liu@finexcorp.com, security@finexcorp.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Potential exposure of logs referencing FinexCorp PII — initial notice

Hi Aditya,

I wanted to alert you to a potential exposure we discovered this morning during internal monitoring. Our ingestion pipeline ingested a subset of application logs that appear to contain hashed customer identifiers and several lines that reference email addresses in plain text. At this stage we do not have evidence of exfiltration, but we need to treat this as a potential incident.

Can Redwood confirm whether any requests from FinexCorp environments could have included logs or payloads that would be stored by Redwood subprocessors within the last 72 hours? Specifically:
- Which subprocessors handled payload processing for FinexCorp between 2027-03-30 and 2027-04-02?
- Can you provide a timestamped audit of retention locations and any backing store identifiers?
- Do you have a secure mechanism for us to receive logs/evidence (we prefer a short-lived S3 presigned or secure Drive folder)?

Per our DPA (section 9.1) we’re beginning our incident timeline and will escalate per contract if significant data is confirmed. Please treat this as urgent — our security and legal teams are standing by.

Thanks in advance,

Alice Zhang
Security Incident Response
FinexCorp

Attachments: finex_initial_alert.pdf (summary of findings)
From: aditya_rao@redwood.example.com
To: Alice Zhang <alice@finexcorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential exposure of logs referencing FinexCorp PII — initial notice

Alice — thanks for the heads up and for the PDF. We take these reports seriously. Quick answers up front:
- I’m escalating to our incident response + legal immediately (cc’d).
- We will provide a list of active subprocessors and any retention locations for the 72-hour window.
- For evidence transfer we can provision a short-lived secure bucket (S3 with customer-supplied KMS or Redwood-managed key) and a Drive link; please confirm your preference.

Next steps we propose:
1) Redwood to publish an initial containment statement within 2 business hours confirming whether any FinexCorp tokens reached our processing pipeline and which subprocessors were touched.
2) Secure evidence handover via a presigned S3 link (expires 7 days) unless you request otherwise.
3) Redwood to produce a scoped log export and subprocessor access logs within 5 business days; if additional forensic traces are required we’ll coordinate scope and a mutually agreeable timeline.

Please share any specific legal requirements (e.g., redaction rules, PCI/SOC2 artifacts) and I’ll make sure our team includes them.

Aditya Rao
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.example.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

--
Attachment: redwood_evidence_instructions.txt (instructions for secure upload)
From: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
To: aditya_rao@redwood.example.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
Cc: (internal)
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: FinexCorp — coord on subprocessor logs & DPA timelines

Folks — looping in internal ops/legal action items so we have a clear plan. Notes:
- Contract reference: FinexCorp DPA (v2025) — see clause 7.2 (Incident notification windows) and clause 4.3 (subprocessor details). They expect initial notification and reasonable cooperation, but language around evidence handover is negotiable.
- Proposed SLOs for our side:
  * Initial confirmation (yes/no) of pipeline touch within 2 hours of Aditya’s notice (we can do this).
  * A scoped export (redacted where appropriate) of processing logs + subprocessor access audit within 72 hours.
  * Full forensic package within 10 business days if requested by Finex legal.

We should avoid committing to broad retention retrieval unless legal sanctions require it. Instead, offer a scoped export limited to relevant keys, time windows, and subprocessor nodes.

Action items:
- Neha: please draft the cooperation letter referencing DPA clauses and propose the timeline above as our default. Include the standard limits on data types we will disclose (no production backups without court order).
- Aditya: confirm the list of subprocessors and whether we can capture access logs from PartnerX for the dates requested.
- Ops: prepare a subprocessor_log_snapshot.csv with per-node timestamps and indicate if any cached kv-entries include candidate PII.

Attachments: subprocessor_log_snapshot.csv (stub)

-Marissa
Director, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
From: aditya_rao@redwood.example.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.example.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.example.com
Cc: Alice Zhang <alice@finexcorp.com>, security@finexcorp.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential exposure of logs referencing FinexCorp PII — initial notice

Marissa / Neha — status update for Finex:
- Subprocessors touched in the 72-hour window: PartnerX (transcoding), LogStoreCo (transient buffering), EdgeOps (ingest edge). I confirmed with infra that cached KV entries are rotated every 24 hours; nothing indicates long-term retention beyond policy.
- Ops will deliver the scoped CSV within the hour to the secure bucket. I have provisioned an S3 presigned transfer link and a Drive folder; I put the link below and set expiration to 7 days. We will encrypt with a Redwood-managed KMS key unless Finex requests to use their key.

Secure upload link: https://app.redwood.example.com/secure-evidence-transfer/FINEX-2027-04-02 (one-time upload portal)
Drive mirror: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bExampleSecureUpload

Neha — please send the cooperation letter and the DPA clause extract to Alice and attach our standard limits (no full backups, no raw customer PII beyond scoped extracts) so Finex’s legal team can review.

Aditya

On a separate note: ops reports there are 14 candidate lines in a transient buffer that reference email-like strings; we will include a redacted sample in the upload rather than full addresses unless legal directs otherwise.
From: Alice Zhang <alice@finexcorp.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.example.com
Cc: tom.liu@finexcorp.com, security@finexcorp.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential exposure of logs referencing FinexCorp PII — initial notice

Aditya / Marissa / Neha — thank you for the rapid response and for provisioning the transfer links. Finex prefers Redwood-managed KMS for the initial transfer; we'll request a customer-managed key only if we escalate to forensic export.

We received the CSV stub and the redacted sample. Next steps from our side: legal will review the cooperation letter and we will provide a signed acceptance of the proposed timeline or request adjustments within 24 hours.

Appreciate the clear boundaries on backups and scope. We will open a secure channel for any follow-up evidence requests and will reach out if we need a full forensic package.

Best,
Alice
Security Incident Response
FinexCorp
